meta.title: Computer Science, Computer Systems & System Design — 60-Week Guided Curriculum
meta.profile: Cybersecurity/threat-intelligence engineer with practical Python, Airflow, Kafka, MongoDB, Linux and networking experience

phases.name: Baseline, decomposition and learning system
phases.university_influence: Caltech project discipline + MIT 6.033 design writing
phases.goal: Establish evidence-based starting level, repository structure, debugging habits and a mandatory decomposition protocol.

phases.name: Programming abstractions and software construction
phases.goal: Move beyond framework-driven coding into recursion, abstraction, multiple paradigms, interpreters, testing and clear module contracts.

phases.name: Discrete mathematics, probability and proof
phases.university_influence: Berkeley CS 70 + MIT Mathematics for Computer Science + Caltech CS 18/21
phases.goal: Develop the ability to prove correctness, reason with invariants, quantify uncertainty and analyze recursive structures.

phases.name: Data structures and algorithms
phases.goal: Choose and implement data structures from workload requirements, prove algorithm correctness and measure rather than guess performance.

phases.name: Machine structures and computer architecture
phases.university_influence: Berkeley CS 61C + Stanford CS 107 + Caltech CS 24
phases.goal: Understand how source code becomes machine execution, including memory, assembly, linking, caches, virtual memory and parallelism.

phases.name: Operating systems and systems programming
phases.goal: Reason about processes, concurrency, virtual memory, persistence, I/O and failure at the operating-system boundary.

phases.name: Database systems
phases.goal: Understand databases as systems: pages, indexes, query execution, transactions, concurrency control and recovery.

phases.name: Networking and security
phases.goal: Trace real network behavior, implement reliable transport concepts and design systems with explicit security boundaries.

phases.name: Distributed systems, system design and capstone
phases.goal: Design, implement, test and defend a fault-aware threat-intelligence system using measurable guarantees.

weeks.title: Baseline diagnostic and curriculum setup
weeks.language: Python, C, Java and technical writing
knowledge: Establish baseline in programming, data structures, proofs, C, Linux and architecture.
Create a reproducible learning repository and progress record.
weeks.decomposition: For each diagnostic problem, write inputs, outputs, constraints, examples, edge cases, state and test oracles before coding.
work: Complete a 90-minute mixed diagnostic: one Python transformation, one linked-structure problem, one proof, one C memory trace and one systems-design prompt.
Create the repository layout from this curriculum.
Record confidence before each answer and compare confidence with results.
weeks.deliverable: baseline.md with scores, misconceptions, evidence and a personalized no-skip/compress decision for every phase.
success: Every score has linked evidence.
At least three false-confidence areas are identified.
No phase is skipped solely because the topic feels familiar.

weeks.title: Problem specification, decomposition and testing
knowledge: Contracts, invariants, state transitions and failure surfaces.
Test design from requirements rather than code branches.
weeks.decomposition: Use the fixed ladder: restate → examples → constraints → state → invariants → interfaces → failures → tests → complexity.
work: Specify an IOC normalizer, a rate limiter and a duplicate-event suppressor without coding first.
Produce two different decompositions for one problem and compare coupling.
Implement only after the design is reviewed by the tutor.
weeks.deliverable: Three DESIGN.md files plus a small tested implementation of the duplicate-event suppressor.
success: Every requirement maps to a test.
Components can be tested independently.
Rejected alternatives are documented with reasons.

weeks.title: Expressions, functions and environment models
knowledge: Pure functions, side effects and referential transparency.
weeks.decomposition: Represent a program as transformations with explicit inputs and outputs before introducing shared state.
work: Follow CS 61A opening lectures/readings.
Trace ten expression evaluations by hand.
Refactor a monolithic enrichment script into composable functions.
weeks.deliverable: A pure-function IOC normalization pipeline with unit tests and evaluation traces.
success: Can explain every binding and return value.
Core transformations have no hidden I/O.
Tests include malformed and adversarial inputs.

weeks.title: Recursion and recursive problem decomposition
knowledge: Recursive definitions, base cases and progress measures.
weeks.decomposition: For each recursive function state: smaller subproblem, base case, combination step and termination measure.
work: Solve recursive sequence, tree and partition problems.
Draw call trees before running code.
Rewrite one recursive solution iteratively and compare invariants.
weeks.deliverable: Recursive domain-tree analyzer for subdomains or URL paths.
success: No recursion without a stated termination argument.
Can estimate call-tree growth.
Can explain when recursion clarifies or obscures the solution.

weeks.title: Higher-order functions and abstraction barriers
knowledge: Functions as values, closures and decorators.
weeks.decomposition: Identify the varying policy and pass it through an interface instead of duplicating control flow.
work: Build reusable map/filter/fold-style transformations.
Implement configurable scoring and filtering policies for indicators.
Create property-based-style test cases without requiring a library.
weeks.deliverable: Policy-driven IOC scoring pipeline with interchangeable scoring functions.
success: Adding a policy does not modify the engine.
Representation details do not leak into callers.
Can explain closure-captured state precisely.

weeks.title: Data abstraction, objects and mutation
knowledge: Abstract data types and representation invariants.
weeks.decomposition: State who owns mutable data, who may mutate it and what invariant each method preserves.
work: Implement a bounded cache as an ADT.
Create aliasing bugs deliberately and diagnose them.
Compare functional and mutable designs for an enrichment cache.
weeks.deliverable: Thread-unsafe bounded cache with rigorous sequential invariants and tests; concurrency comes later.
success: Representation invariant is checked in tests.
Public API does not expose mutable internals.
Can identify all aliases to mutable state.

weeks.title: Functional programming, Scheme and interpreters
knowledge: Symbolic expressions, lexical scope and evaluation.
Functional recursion over lists and trees.
Interpreter loop: parse, evaluate and apply.
weeks.decomposition: Separate syntax representation, environment, evaluation rules and primitive operations.
work: Complete selected CS 61A Scheme exercises.
Trace lexical versus dynamic scope examples.
Implement a tiny expression evaluator in Python.
weeks.deliverable: Mini interpreter supporting numbers, names, arithmetic, definitions and conditionals.
success: Can trace environment frames by hand.
Parser and evaluator are independently tested.
Errors are represented deliberately rather than as accidental crashes.

weeks.title: Declarative programming, SQL and phase project
knowledge: Module boundaries, test doubles and integration tests.
weeks.decomposition: Describe desired result before execution strategy; isolate persistence from domain logic.
work: Complete selected CS 61A SQL work.
Build a small SQLite-backed indicator catalog.
Run an oral review covering recursion, abstraction, mutation and interpreter design.
weeks.deliverable: Phase project: local IOC catalog with import, normalization, scoring, querying and a written architecture.
success: All external I/O is behind interfaces.
Database schema reflects explicit invariants.
Tutor score is at least 10/12 with no zero category.

weeks.title: Logic, sets and proof structure
weeks.decomposition: Translate informal claims into quantified statements before attempting a proof.
work: Work MIT MCS/CS 70 logic and set exercises.
Find counterexamples to five plausible but false engineering claims.
Encode small finite checks in Python without treating experiments as proofs.
weeks.deliverable: proof-journal-01.md with eight complete proofs and counterexamples.
success: Quantifiers are explicit.
Proof steps cite definitions or prior facts.
Can explain why testing many cases is not a general proof.

weeks.title: Induction, recursion and invariants
knowledge: Loop invariants, initialization, maintenance and termination.
weeks.decomposition: Choose an induction parameter or invariant that matches the program's state transition.
work: Prove correctness of binary search and one recursive tree function.
Derive an invariant for a streaming deduplicator.
Find the smallest counterexample to a broken invariant.
weeks.deliverable: Correctness note for two programs, including termination and complexity.
success: Invariant is true initially and preserved.
Termination is argued separately from partial correctness.
Can connect recursive code to an inductive proof.

weeks.title: Graphs, relations and state machines
knowledge: Directed and undirected graphs, paths, connectivity and trees.
weeks.decomposition: Model entities, transitions and forbidden states before choosing an algorithm.
work: Model an IOC lifecycle as a state machine.
Prove two unreachable states under the proposed transition rules.
Solve graph-theory exercises from MIT MCS/CS 70.
weeks.deliverable: State-machine specification with diagram, transition table, invariants and executable validator.
success: All transitions name preconditions and effects.
Illegal transitions are rejected.
Can distinguish graph model from traversal algorithm.

weeks.title: Number theory and cryptographic reasoning
knowledge: Fast exponentiation and basic public-key structure.
Difference between mathematical primitive and secure protocol.
weeks.decomposition: Separate algebraic correctness, computational cost and security assumptions.
work: Implement Euclid and modular exponentiation.
Work modular-arithmetic proofs.
Explain why textbook RSA-like arithmetic alone is not a complete secure system.
weeks.deliverable: Number-theory notebook plus a security-assumptions memo.
success: Can compute and justify modular inverses.
Fast exponentiation complexity is derived.
No claim confuses correctness with security.

weeks.title: Counting and discrete probability
knowledge: Conditional probability, independence and Bayes' rule.
weeks.decomposition: Define the experiment and sample space before applying formulas.
work: Solve counting and conditional-probability problems.
Analyze false-positive rates for a multi-provider IOC workflow.
Use simulation only to validate, not replace, an analytic result.
weeks.deliverable: Probability analysis of a threat-intelligence alert pipeline.
success: Events and conditioning are explicit.
Independence is justified, not assumed.
Simulation converges near the analytic result.

weeks.title: Random variables, expectation, recurrences and asymptotics
knowledge: Recurrences, growth rates and asymptotic notation.
weeks.decomposition: Choose a cost variable, derive its recurrence or expectation, then test the model empirically.
work: Analyze hashing and retry costs.
Solve recurrences by expansion/substitution.
Complete a closed-book phase assessment.
weeks.deliverable: Math gate packet: proofs, probability model, recurrence analysis and corrections.
success: Can derive rather than memorize common bounds.
Can use expectation without assuming independence where unnecessary.
Assessment reaches 80% and every error has a corrected explanation.

weeks.title: Java, static types, references and testing
knowledge: Static typing, classes, interfaces and references.
Unit tests, assertions and test isolation.
weeks.decomposition: Define the ADT and tests before selecting fields or implementation classes.
work: Complete selected CS 61B Java introduction work.
Port the bounded cache API to Java.
Write tests before implementation for one component.
weeks.deliverable: Java project skeleton with CI, tests and style checks.
success: Public interfaces contain no implementation details.
Equality semantics are explicit.
Tests fail for the intended reasons before code is added.

weeks.title: Linked lists, deques and representation invariants
knowledge: Sentinels, boundary cases and iterator state.
weeks.decomposition: Draw the representation and state every pointer invariant before implementing updates.
work: Implement linked deque from a specification.
Test empty, singleton and mutation sequences.
Perform code review focused on invariants and aliasing.
weeks.deliverable: LinkedDeque with iterator, randomized differential tests and invariant checker.
success: Every mutation preserves forward/backward links.
No special-case explosion at boundaries.
Iterator behavior under mutation is documented.

weeks.title: Resizable arrays, generics and API design
weeks.decomposition: Separate logical sequence behavior from storage-capacity policy.
work: Implement array deque.
Prove amortized append cost informally with aggregate analysis.
Compare memory locality with linked representation.
weeks.deliverable: ArrayDeque and a benchmark comparing both deque implementations.
success: Capacity never violates stated bounds.
Benchmark methodology is reproducible.
Can explain why asymptotic equality does not imply equal performance.

weeks.title: Trees, search trees and balanced indexing
weeks.decomposition: State ordering invariant and define each operation as a transformation preserving it.
work: Implement BST map.
Trace worst-case degeneration.
Work selected CS 61B tree exercises and compare BST with B-tree page behavior.
weeks.deliverable: BST-based IOC map with traversal, deletion tests and shape analysis.
success: Ordering invariant is tested.
Can explain height-dependent complexity.
Deletion cases are decomposed and verified independently.

weeks.title: Hash tables, sets and workload-driven choices
knowledge: Hash functions, collisions, load factor and resizing.
weeks.decomposition: Begin with required operations, key distribution and memory limits; then choose collision strategy.
work: Implement a hash map.
Generate collision-heavy keys.
Compare hash, tree and sorted-array approaches for IOC lookup.
weeks.deliverable: Hash map plus workload decision record.
success: Resizing preserves all entries.
Collision tests are deliberate.
Complexity claims list their assumptions.

weeks.title: Heaps, priority queues and disjoint sets
knowledge: Union-find, path compression and union by rank/size.
Model reduction: solving one problem through another ADT.
weeks.decomposition: Identify the exact operation mix and map the domain problem to an existing abstract data type.
work: Implement binary heap.
Use union-find for a connectivity problem.
Build a priority-based enrichment scheduler.
weeks.deliverable: Scheduler plus connectivity lab and complexity notes.
success: Heap operations preserve shape and order.
Can explain amortized union-find behavior conceptually.
Domain mapping is documented before implementation.

weeks.title: Sorting, selection and empirical algorithm analysis
knowledge: Insertion, merge, quick and heap sort.
Stability, in-place behavior and lower-bound intuition.
weeks.decomposition: Define data distributions, metrics and hypotheses before benchmarking.
work: Implement or instrument multiple sorting algorithms.
Benchmark random, sorted, reverse and duplicate-heavy inputs.
Explain discrepancies between theoretical and measured behavior.
weeks.deliverable: Sorting laboratory with plots, raw data and interpretation.
success: Correctness is tested separately from speed.
Warm-up and repeated measurements are used.
No chart is presented without workload details.

weeks.title: Graph traversal, topological order and components
weeks.decomposition: Define graph representation and the meaning of visited state before traversal.
work: Implement BFS/DFS.
Model provider dependencies as a directed graph.
Detect cycles and produce valid execution order when possible.
weeks.deliverable: Dependency-graph analyzer with explanations for cycles.
success: Traversal complexity includes representation cost.
Cycle evidence is returned, not only a boolean.
Can state the queue/stack invariant.

weeks.title: Shortest paths and minimum spanning trees
knowledge: Unweighted shortest path, Dijkstra and negative-weight limitations.
Minimum spanning trees and greedy-choice reasoning.
weeks.decomposition: Match weight semantics and constraints to the algorithm; reject invalid choices explicitly.
work: Implement Dijkstra with a priority queue.
Construct a counterexample for Dijkstra with negative edges.
Solve a network-cost MST problem.
weeks.deliverable: Path-analysis service with algorithm-selection ADR.
success: Relaxation is explained precisely.
Invalid input assumptions are checked.
Can distinguish shortest-path tree from MST.

weeks.title: Algorithm paradigms and phase project
knowledge: Divide and conquer, greedy design and dynamic programming.
Subproblem graphs, optimal substructure and memoization.
Correctness argument as part of design.
weeks.decomposition: Define state, transition, base cases and evaluation order before writing a dynamic program.
work: Solve one divide-and-conquer, one greedy and two DP problems.
Build a content-addressed IOC history store or compact Git-like snapshot project.
Complete oral algorithm review.
weeks.deliverable: Phase project with design document, tests, benchmark and correctness explanation.
success: Algorithm choice is justified against alternatives.
Project uses at least four studied data structures appropriately.
Tutor gate score is at least 10/12 with no zero.

weeks.title: C execution model, pointers and memory ownership
knowledge: Compilation units, types, arrays and pointer arithmetic.
weeks.decomposition: For every allocation, record owner, aliases, valid lifetime and release point.
work: Complete selected Beej/61C C work.
Implement strings and dynamic arrays without unsafe shortcuts.
Diagnose seeded memory bugs with GDB and sanitizers.
weeks.deliverable: C utility library with ownership documentation and tests.
success: No sanitizer findings.
Can draw stack/heap state at key calls.
No pointer operation is justified by guessing.

weeks.title: Bits, integers, floating point and data representation
knowledge: Two's complement, bit operations and overflow.
weeks.decomposition: Specify bit layout, valid range and conversion rules before manipulating representations.
work: Implement bit-field utilities.
Serialize a compact indicator record with explicit endianness.
Investigate integer and floating-point edge cases.
weeks.deliverable: Portable binary record format with encoder, decoder and golden tests.
success: Round trips preserve valid values.
Malformed encodings are rejected.
Can explain signed overflow and floating-point comparison hazards.

weeks.title: RISC-V assembly and calling conventions
knowledge: Stack frames, calling convention and recursion.
weeks.decomposition: Track live values, register ownership and stack-frame layout at every call boundary.
work: Translate small C functions to RISC-V.
Trace recursive assembly by hand.
Inspect compiler-generated assembly at different optimization levels.
weeks.deliverable: Annotated assembly notebook and two hand-written functions.
success: Calling convention is respected.
Can recover high-level control flow from assembly.
Can explain compiler optimizations observed.

weeks.title: Compilation, linking, object files and loaders
knowledge: Symbols, relocations, static and dynamic libraries.
weeks.decomposition: Treat build output as a graph of artifacts and symbol dependencies.
work: Create multi-file static and shared-library builds.
Inspect symbols and sections with binutils.
Trigger and diagnose compile-time, link-time and load-time failures.
weeks.deliverable: Build-and-link laboratory with diagrams and failure catalog.
success: Can distinguish declaration, definition and symbol visibility.
Can explain relocation at a conceptual level.
Build is reproducible from one command.

weeks.title: Digital logic, datapaths and instruction execution
knowledge: Boolean logic, combinational and sequential elements.
weeks.decomposition: Split behavior into state elements, combinational transformations and control signals.
work: Work selected 61C datapath exercises.
Trace instructions through a simple CPU.
Optionally complete Nand2Tetris logic/CPU projects.
weeks.deliverable: Single-cycle CPU explanation with annotated datapath.
success: Can identify all state changes for an instruction.
Control signals are derived from semantics.
Can explain what the ISA hides from software.

weeks.title: Pipelining and performance reasoning
knowledge: Pipeline stages, hazards, forwarding and stalls.
weeks.decomposition: Identify the critical path, parallel stages and dependency hazards before proposing optimization.
work: Trace pipeline schedules.
Calculate speedup limits.
Optimize a small C workload and measure before/after.
weeks.deliverable: Performance report with hypothesis, profile, change and evidence.
success: Optimization targets measured bottleneck.
Pipeline hazards are identified correctly.
No speedup claim omits baseline and workload.

weeks.title: Caches, locality and memory hierarchy
knowledge: Cache lines, mapping, associativity and replacement.
weeks.decomposition: Model access pattern first; then predict hits, misses and bandwidth needs.
work: Solve cache-address exercises.
Benchmark row/column traversal and structure layouts.
Use a profiler to connect code to cache behavior.
weeks.deliverable: Cache-locality laboratory using an IOC parsing workload.
success: Can calculate set/tag/offset.
Measured behavior matches or corrects prediction.
Optimization preserves readability or documents the trade-off.

weeks.title: Virtual memory, parallelism and architecture gate
knowledge: Address translation, page tables and TLBs.
weeks.decomposition: Trace virtual address → translation → permission → physical access; identify shared cache lines in parallel designs.
work: Inspect process mappings and page faults.
Use mmap for a file-backed dataset.
Run a small false-sharing experiment and complete phase assessment.
weeks.deliverable: Machine-structures gate packet and cache-aware binary IOC reader.
success: Can explain translation and protection without hand-waving.
Reader handles malformed files safely.
Gate score is at least 10/12 with no zero.

weeks.title: Operating-system roles, abstractions and system calls
knowledge: OS as resource manager, isolation boundary and service provider.
User/kernel mode, traps and system calls.
Processes, threads, files and sockets as abstractions.
weeks.decomposition: For each abstraction name hidden mechanism, exposed contract, policy decisions and failure modes.
work: Watch opening CS 162 lectures.
Trace selected programs with strace.
Map one Python operation to library and system calls.
weeks.deliverable: os-abstractions.md grounded in the learner's Linux/Proxmox environment.
success: Can distinguish library call from syscall.
Can explain protection boundary.
Every abstraction includes failure examples.

weeks.title: Processes, fork, exec, wait and signals
weeks.decomposition: Model process creation as state transitions and track inherited resources explicitly.
work: Implement fork/exec examples.
Observe copy-on-write and descriptor inheritance.
Handle child status and signals correctly.
weeks.deliverable: Process laboratory plus the first version of a miniature shell.
success: No zombies remain.
Exit status propagates correctly.
Can predict parent/child memory and descriptor behavior.

weeks.title: File descriptors, pipes and shell execution
weeks.decomposition: Separate parsing, execution plan, descriptor wiring, process lifecycle and error reporting.
work: Add redirection and pipelines to the shell.
Draw descriptor state before/after dup2.
Test missing commands, permissions and broken pipes.
weeks.deliverable: Mini shell with pipelines, redirection and integration tests.
success: Unused pipe ends are closed.
No hangs from leaked descriptors.
Parser and executor are independently testable.

weeks.title: Threads, races and nondeterminism
knowledge: Thread stacks and shared address space.
weeks.decomposition: For every shared variable name owner, readers, writers and synchronization requirement.
work: Create a race deliberately.
Enumerate possible interleavings.
Build unsafe then safe parallel file hashing.
weeks.deliverable: Race-condition incident report with reproduction and correction.
success: Race is reproducible under stress.
Shared state inventory is complete.
Can distinguish data race from higher-level race condition.

weeks.title: Locks, condition variables and semaphores
weeks.decomposition: Write the synchronization predicate and invariant before selecting a primitive.
work: Implement bounded producer-consumer queue.
Use randomized schedules and sanitizers.
Prove queue safety properties informally.
weeks.deliverable: Concurrent IOC-enrichment work queue.
success: No data race or deadlock in stress tests.
Condition waits use predicate loops.
Queue invariants are documented and tested.

weeks.title: Deadlock, scheduling and liveness
knowledge: Deadlock conditions, wait-for graphs and lock ordering.
weeks.decomposition: Construct resource graph and measurable scheduling objective before proposing a policy.
work: Create and fix a deadlock.
Simulate FCFS, round-robin and priority scheduling.
Analyze mixed CPU/I/O workloads.
weeks.deliverable: Scheduling simulator and concurrency postmortem.
success: Can identify all four deadlock conditions.
Fix preserves required concurrency.
Performance claims use multiple workloads.

weeks.title: Address spaces, paging and replacement
knowledge: Virtual pages, page tables, TLB and protection.
Demand paging, working sets and page faults.
weeks.decomposition: Define address-reference workload and success metric before comparing replacement policies.
work: Inspect Linux mappings/faults.
Implement a page-replacement simulator.
Construct a Belady-anomaly case.
weeks.deliverable: Virtual-memory experiment with hand-worked validation.
success: Simulator matches known traces.
Can distinguish capacity from locality issue.
Can explain copy-on-write.

weeks.title: File systems, naming and storage layout
knowledge: Inodes, directories, links and path resolution.
Allocation, metadata, caching and free-space management.
weeks.decomposition: State persistent invariants and separate naming, metadata and data placement.
work: Explore links and inode behavior.
Implement directory traversal.
Measure sequential/random file access.
weeks.deliverable: Filesystem explorer and storage-path diagram.
success: Can distinguish inode from pathname.
Traversal handles cycles and errors.
Measurements explain device/cache effects cautiously.

weeks.title: Crash consistency, journaling and durable updates
knowledge: Write ordering, atomic rename and fsync.
weeks.decomposition: Enumerate every crash point between persistent state transitions.
work: Build crash-safe snapshot writer.
Inject process termination between writes.
Document which guarantees depend on filesystem/hardware assumptions.
weeks.deliverable: Crash-safe IOC snapshot service with recovery tests.
success: No partial snapshot becomes visible.
Recovery is idempotent.
Durability claims are precise and bounded.

weeks.title: Sockets, OS integration and systems gate
knowledge: Integration of processes, threads, memory and persistence.
weeks.decomposition: Separate protocol, connection lifecycle, worker model, state ownership and shutdown.
work: Build a local TCP service around the work queue and snapshot store.
Test disconnects, partial reads and shutdown.
Complete oral OS defense.
weeks.deliverable: Systems project: networked IOC ingestion daemon with graceful shutdown and durable snapshots.
success: Protocol handles framing and partial I/O.
Failure tests cover process crash and client disconnect.
Gate score is at least 10/12 with no zero.

weeks.title: Relational model, SQL and query plans
knowledge: Relations, keys, constraints and normalization trade-offs.
weeks.decomposition: Start from required questions and invariants; derive schema and indexes afterward.
work: Model an IOC/detection dataset.
Write analytical queries.
Inspect SQLite/PostgreSQL query plans.
weeks.deliverable: Schema, representative workload and query-plan notebook.
success: Constraints encode domain rules.
Queries have expected-result tests.
Indexes are not added without a target query.

weeks.title: Pages, records and buffer pools
weeks.language: C++ reading + Python or C++ implementation
knowledge: Heap files, slotted pages and record layout.
Buffer-pool pinning, dirty pages and eviction.
Durability boundary between memory and disk.
weeks.decomposition: Separate page format, disk manager, cache policy and concurrency concerns.
work: Study CMU storage lectures.
Implement fixed-size pages and a small buffer pool.
Inject full-disk and corrupt-page failures.
weeks.deliverable: Page-based mini storage manager.
success: Records survive restart.
Page invariants are tested.
Eviction policy is replaceable.

weeks.title: B+ trees and hash indexes
knowledge: Fan-out, page splits and ordered scans.
weeks.decomposition: Define supported predicates and page-size constraints before choosing index structure.
work: Implement a simplified paged B+ tree or complete selected BusTub work locally.
Test splits and root changes.
Compare point lookup and range scan.
weeks.deliverable: Index module plus invariant checker.
success: Search returns correct results after repeated splits.
Leaf ordering and linkage invariants hold.
Choice is justified from query workload.

weeks.title: Query execution, joins and optimization
weeks.decomposition: Represent a query as operators with contracts, then identify dominant data movement.
work: Implement simple operators over pages.
Compare join strategies on controlled datasets.
Explain one PostgreSQL planner decision.
weeks.deliverable: Mini query executor and benchmark report.
success: Operators compose through a stable interface.
Join output is tested against SQL reference.
Cost explanation includes cardinality assumptions.

weeks.title: Transactions, isolation and concurrency control
weeks.decomposition: State required invariant and acceptable visibility per operation before choosing isolation level.
work: Reproduce dirty/non-repeatable/phantom-style behaviors where supported.
Analyze concurrent IOC updates.
Design lock or MVCC behavior for the mini engine.
weeks.deliverable: Isolation laboratory and concurrency-control design.
success: Can distinguish application invariant from DB guarantee.
Anomalies are shown with precise schedules.
Chosen isolation level is justified per workflow.

weeks.title: WAL, recovery and database gate
weeks.decomposition: Model transaction states and crash points; derive recovery actions from persisted evidence.
work: Add a simple WAL to the storage manager.
Inject crashes before/after log and data writes.
Select final capstone scope and freeze its core guarantees.
weeks.deliverable: Recoverable mini storage engine and capstone proposal.
success: Committed data survives restart.
Uncommitted effects are absent or undone as designed.
Gate score is at least 10/12 with no zero.

weeks.title: Ethernet, IP, routing and the packet path
knowledge: Layering, frames, packets, addressing and forwarding.
ARP/neighbor discovery, routing tables and TTL.
weeks.decomposition: Trace each hop and name state consulted, header changes and failure outcomes.
work: Study CS 144 opening material.
Capture and annotate traffic.
Trace packets across host, router/NAT and destination.
weeks.deliverable: Packet-path report grounded in the home lab.
success: Can explain L2 versus L3 decisions.
Header fields are interpreted correctly.
NAT and routing are not conflated.

weeks.title: Reliable transport, flow and congestion control
knowledge: Sliding windows, flow control and congestion control.
weeks.decomposition: Define sender/receiver state, invariants, timer behavior and duplicate handling.
work: Implement selected CS 144 byte-stream/TCP concepts locally.
Simulate loss, reordering and duplication.
Explain exactly-once illusions over an unreliable network.
weeks.deliverable: Reliable-stream component with adversarial tests.
success: Data is delivered in order without duplication.
Window and sequence arithmetic are tested at boundaries.
Timeout behavior is deterministic under a fake clock.

weeks.title: DNS, HTTP, TLS and service architecture
knowledge: HTTP semantics, proxies and load balancing.
TLS handshake, certificates and trust boundaries.
weeks.decomposition: Separate naming, transport security, application semantics and deployment topology.
work: Trace DNS and TLS for a controlled domain.
Build a small HTTP service behind a reverse proxy.
Document caching and retry implications.
weeks.deliverable: End-to-end request trace and service topology.
success: Can locate trust decisions in TLS.
Can distinguish HTTP retry safety by method/operation.
Caching behavior is explicit.

weeks.title: Security principles, threat modeling and memory safety
knowledge: Assets, adversaries, trust boundaries and attack surfaces.
Least privilege, defense in depth and complete mediation.
Memory corruption and exploit primitives conceptually.
weeks.decomposition: Threat model each interface: asset, attacker capability, entry point, control and residual risk.
work: Study CS 161 introduction and memory-safety units.
Audit the C ingestion daemon.
Create exploit-oriented tests without writing harmful deployment code.
weeks.deliverable: Threat model and secure redesign for the ingestion daemon.
success: Trust boundaries are diagrammed.
Controls map to explicit threats.
Residual risks and assumptions are acknowledged.

weeks.title: Cryptography, authentication and web security
knowledge: Injection, XSS, CSRF, session and authorization failures.
weeks.decomposition: Choose primitives only after defining authenticity, confidentiality, freshness and authorization requirements.
work: Complete selected CS 161 crypto/web units.
Design signed provider updates.
Audit a small API for injection and authorization failures.
weeks.deliverable: Authenticated update protocol and web/API security checklist.
success: No custom cryptographic primitive is invented.
Replay handling is explicit.
Authentication and authorization are separated.

weeks.title: Network security and secure-service gate
knowledge: Network segmentation, firewall limits and shared infrastructure.
Secure logging, rate limits and abuse resistance.
weeks.decomposition: Define allowed flows, identities, trust zones, abuse cases and failure behavior.
work: Build a secure telemetry collector with TLS/authentication, bounded queues and audit logs.
Test malformed clients, replay, overload and dependency failure.
Complete security/network oral review.
weeks.deliverable: Secure collector integrated with the storage engine.
success: Overload is bounded rather than catastrophic.
Logs avoid secrets while preserving evidence.
Gate score is at least 10/12 with no zero.

weeks.title: Distributed failures, time, RPC and idempotency
knowledge: RPC semantics, deadlines, retries and duplicate requests.
weeks.decomposition: For each operation enumerate request loss, response loss, duplication, reordering, timeout and retry.
work: Learn required Go basics.
Complete/adapt MIT 6.5840 MapReduce or key/value introductory lab.
Add idempotency to one capstone operation.
weeks.deliverable: Failure matrix and retry-safe API implementation.
success: Every retry policy has a bound.
Duplicate effects are prevented or detected.
Can explain why timeout does not reveal operation outcome.

weeks.title: Replication, consistency and quorums
weeks.decomposition: Specify consistency per operation and user-visible anomaly before choosing replication.
work: Analyze consistency needs of indicator updates versus analytics.
Simulate replicas with delay and failure.
Write consistency tests as histories.
weeks.deliverable: Replication prototype and consistency contract.
success: Consistency terms are used precisely.
Tests include stale reads and failover.
Trade-off is tied to product behavior.

weeks.title: Consensus and Raft
knowledge: Leader election, log replication and safety.
Terms, commit index and majority reasoning.
weeks.decomposition: Model node state and message handlers as a state machine; test safety under reordered events.
work: Read the Raft paper.
Implement/adapt the first Raft stages from MIT 6.5840.
Use deterministic simulation or controlled tests.
weeks.deliverable: Raft implementation notes, state diagram and passing safety tests.
success: Election safety and log matching are explainable.
Persistent state survives restart.
No correctness argument depends on timing alone.

weeks.title: Partitioning, streams and distributed transactions
knowledge: Event ordering, consumer groups and idempotent processing.
Sagas, two-phase commit and atomic-outbox pattern.
weeks.decomposition: Define atomicity boundary, ordering scope and recovery action for each multi-component workflow.
work: Design partitioning for telemetry/IOC workloads.
Implement idempotent event consumption with an outbox or equivalent.
Inject duplicates and consumer restarts.
weeks.deliverable: Capstone event pipeline with recovery tests.
success: Partition key follows access pattern.
Consumer replay is safe.
Cross-system invariants have an explicit reconciliation strategy.

weeks.title: System design, capacity, SLOs and failure injection
knowledge: SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and observability.
weeks.decomposition: Use a timed design flow: requirements → estimates → model/API → architecture → deep dive → failure/security → recap.
work: Complete an MIT 6.033-style design document.
Define capstone SLOs and capacity model.
Run load and failure-injection experiments.
weeks.deliverable: Final architecture packet: diagrams, ADRs, threat model, capacity model, SLOs and experiment results.
success: Numbers influence architecture.
Critical guarantees have tests.
Unknowns are listed as risks rather than hidden.

weeks.title: Capstone completion, oral defense and next specialization
knowledge: Synthesis across algorithms, architecture, OS, databases, networks, security and distributed systems.
Technical communication and honest limitation analysis.
weeks.decomposition: Freeze scope; map each requirement to component contract, test and evidence.
work: Finish one production-quality vertical slice of the threat-intelligence platform.
Run a clean-room setup from documentation.
Conduct a 60-minute oral defense with an AI tutor and record corrections.
weeks.deliverable: Portfolio capstone: repository, runnable demo, architecture document, ADRs, tests, benchmarks, failure evidence and retrospective.
success: A new engineer can run it from documentation.
At least three failure modes are demonstrated and recovered from.
Final tutor score is at least 10/12 with no zero and every limitation is stated.

university_sources.curriculum: CS/EECS lower division requires CS 61A, 61B, 61C and CS 70; the plan uses these as the primary foundation.
CS fundamentals, mathematical/theoretical intermediate courses and a multi-quarter project sequence motivate the proof and capstone gates.
Programming, systems and algorithmic thinking are combined with system-design subjects; MIT OCW supplies the mathematics, algorithms and design spine.
Programming abstractions, mathematical foundations, computer organization and probability influence the core; CS 144 supplies an open networking laboratory.
Imperative and functional programming, data structures/algorithms, systems, theory and project rigor shape the sequencing and assessment style.
